user.title: Solar Surplus
user.description: The meters the surplus is read from. Consumers are added afterwards, one by one, on the integration's page.

data.grid_export_positive: Grid power is positive when exporting
data.battery_discharge_positive: Battery power is positive when discharging

data_description.grid_power: The meter at the grid connection. By default positive means drawing from the grid.
data_description.battery_power: Optional. By default positive means the battery discharges, as in the energy dashboard. Inverters differ: with no sun and nothing drawn from the grid, the battery discharges, and that tells which way the sensor counts.
data_description.battery_soc: Optional. Without it, what the battery charges with is never handed out.
data_description.battery_target_soc: Below this charge, what the battery charges with is not handed out to consumers.
data_description.battery_min_soc: At or below this charge, drawing from the grid locks SG Ready heat pumps and blocks signals.
data_description.battery_max_charge_power: Optional. Known, the part of it the battery does not use yet is held back for it while it is below the charge above.
data_description.signal_blocked: With the battery empty or none, drawing this much from the grid locks SG Ready heat pumps and blocks signals.
data_description.forecast_entries: Optional. Forecast.Solar, Solcast or any other integration that provides a solar forecast for the energy dashboard. Several are added up.
data_description.reserve: Held back from the surplus. A consumer switches on only if this much is still exported afterwards, and off once the house draws from the grid.
data_description.base_load: What the house draws on its own, to read the forecast with: the expected surplus of an hour is its forecast minus this.

test_mode.title: Test mode
test_mode.description: With the Test mode switch on, nothing is switched. Solar Surplus carries its decisions out in a simulation of the house and sends a notification of what it would have switched.

data_description.notify_target: A notify action or entity, such as your phone's. Left empty, a notification in Home Assistant's sidebar.

switch.title: A switched consumer
switch.description: Switched on and off, such as a heating rod or a smart plug.

data_description.on_delay: How long enough surplus has to hold.
data_description.off_delay: How long too little surplus has to hold.
data_description.power: What it draws when on. Decides whether it fits, and counts as its draw without a power sensor.
data_description.power_sensor: Optional. What it really draws, which is better than the power above once it is on.

number.title: A variable consumer
number.description: Its power is set through a number, such as a wallbox's charging current. It takes all it can get, in steps.

data_description.on_delay: How long enough surplus has to hold.
data_description.off_delay: How long too little surplus has to hold.
data_description.power_sensor: Optional. What it really draws, which is better than the power above once it is on.
data_description.watts_per_unit: 1 for a number in watts, 230 for amperes on one phase, 690 on three.
data_description.switch_entity: Optional. Switched on while it runs, off otherwise.

sg_ready.title: An SG Ready heat pump
sg_ready.description: Two contacts set one of four states: locked, normal, recommended and forced.

data.name: Name
data.sg_lock: Lock while drawing from the grid

data_description.on_delay: How long enough surplus has to hold.
data_description.off_delay: How long too little surplus has to hold.
data_description.power_sensor: Optional. What it really draws, which is better than the power above once it is on.
data_description.sg_forced_power: Optional. Surplus beyond its own power that switches it to forced. Empty, it is never forced.
data_description.sg_lock: Only while the battery is empty, and for at most two hours at a time.

script.title: A consumer with scripts
script.description: Started and stopped through scripts, buttons or scenes.

data_description.on_delay: How long enough surplus has to hold.
data_description.off_delay: How long too little surplus has to hold.
data_description.power: What it draws when on. Decides whether it fits, and counts as its draw without a power sensor.
data_description.power_sensor: Optional. What it really draws, which is better than the power above once it is on.
data_description.state_entity: Optional. Without it, the consumer counts as what it was last told.

deferrable.title: A deferrable consumer
deferrable.description: Waits to be started, such as a washing machine: once ready, it starts as soon as its power fits the surplus, and at the latest so that it is done by its deadline.

data_description.power: What it draws on average while it runs. It starts once this much surplus is there.
data_description.power_sensor: Optional. What it really draws, which is better than the power above once it is on.
data_description.ready_entity: An input boolean is turned off again once the run is done.
data_description.start_entity: A switch is turned on, a script, button or scene is run.
data_description.deadline_entity: Optional. A date and time, or a time of day. Without it, the time below is used.
data_description.deadline_time: The next time of day after it became ready.
data_description.finish_power: With a power sensor, the run is done once it draws less than this for the time below. Without one, once the run time is over.

signal.title: An energy signal
signal.description: Switches nothing. Its own sensor tells blocked, normal, recommended or forced, after the SG Ready states, for another integration to follow, such as the climate control of a heat pump.

data.name: Name
data.sg_lock: Blocked while drawing from the grid

data_description.on_delay: How long enough surplus has to hold.
data_description.off_delay: How long too little surplus has to hold.
data_description.power: What the consumer following it draws extra when recommended.
data_description.power_sensor: Optional. What the consumer following it really draws. Its draw is then counted as the signal's own, so the signal does not switch itself off when it reacts.
data_description.sg_forced_power: Optional. Surplus beyond its own power that makes it forced. Empty, it is never forced.
data_description.sg_lock: Only while the battery is empty, for as long as that lasts.

error.already_controlled: Another consumer is already switched through this entity.
error.same_contact: The two contacts have to be different entities.
error.min_above_power: The minimum power is above the power.

state.on_delay: Waiting for the surplus to hold
state.off_delay: Waiting for the surplus to come back
